soundness_flags.label: ass:cell-support and ass:positive-cell-variance
soundness_flags.one_line: Because q is simplex-valued, its listed probabilities already exhaust the outcome law; moreover eta-interiority at q0 on L distinct support points implies every conditional variance is positive, so both assumptions are redundant.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:local-minimax-lower-bound and thm:feasible-risk-attainment
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The minimax envelope excludes fully sequential, positive-fraction-pilot, and random-limit acquisition rules by restricting to deterministic-limit pilot procedures.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The claimed optimality is conditional on the class mathfrak A_det of vanishing-pilot procedures whose main-wave rates converge locally uniformly to a deterministic feasible design.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:local-chart-membership through thm:feasible-risk-attainment
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The LAN and attainment claims use fixed finite K, M, and L with known finite outcome support and interior cell probabilities.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The identification, Gaussian-game, and attainment conclusions are conditional on the stated fixed finite-support randomized-annotation model.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:certified-computation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Certification is supplied only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic inputs carrying exact validity certificates.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Termination and epsilon-certification are conditional on membership in mathfrak I_rep, not claims for arbitrary opaque real inputs or oracle-free compact sets.

source_verification_receipts.version: Econometrica 77(5), 2009, author-hosted copy of the journal article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper formulates a binary treatment-assignment problem with a scalar welfare contrast and introduces a Gaussian-shift local approximation for regular parametric treatment-rule problems.
The article establishes asymptotic minimax-regret optimality for many treatments and discusses numerical computation of finite-sample rules.
The paper studies two-treatment minimax regret with unknown missing-data distributions, hence partial identification rather than controlled prospective annotation.

source_verification_receipts.version: Econometric Theory 23(1), 2007, author-hosted preprint corresponding to published article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper generalizes incomplete-data minimax-regret treatment choice to finitely many treatments and highlights a three-or-more-treatment phenomenon under ambiguity.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2502.10605v4, 29 July 2026; extended journal version, with page noting preliminary AISTATS 2026 acceptance
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work optimizes annotation probabilities for ATE variance, derives a closed-form allocation, and claims a feasible two-batch estimator with optimal asymptotic variance.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract lines 16-18; Sections 3.1-3.2 and Theorems 1-2 in HTML rendering
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The preprint optimizes semiparametric efficiency for scalar parameters and improves every component of a multidimensional parameter through a maximin two-phase criterion.

The paper studies two-wave experiment design for policy choice, uses Gaussian and quadratic approximations, and requires welfare to be strongly concave near the optimal policy; it distinguishes this from linear finite-arm treatment choice.

The paper studies independent-arm fixed-budget best-arm identification, uses a pilot whose budget fraction vanishes, and attains exact minimax and Bayes simple-regret constants via sequential Gaussian games.
